accepted.reason: The second-pass proposal retains bare повестка for agenda. The standard full equivalent is повестка дня; this also avoids the first-pass calque.

The proposed плотное дорожное движение is a calque; Russian normally says интенсивное/оживлённое движение. This in-band sentence keeps the corrected road-traffic sense without introducing later vocabulary.

after: Check the layout of the rooms.
accepted.reason: The second-pass English says one room's layout while the Russian says the arrangement of multiple rooms. The revised examples express the same spatial arrangement.
The second-pass 'She chose persuasion' remains unnatural in both languages. Russian normally uses уговоры in the plural for persuasion/coaxing.
The second-pass 'suddenly realized' still does not express спохватиться, which implies noticing belatedly and reacting.
The second-pass standalone Он работает чрезмерно is unidiomatic. Чрезмерно много naturally expresses excessive degree while preserving the target adverb.

after: Ms. is used before a surname.
accepted.reason: Госпожа does not encode marital status, so narrowing the gloss to Mrs. is misleading.
The English repair leaves the Russian collocation заполнил опрос; one completes a questionnaire, while one answers a survey/question.
Remove the warmly/well-dressed mismatch using previously taught supporting words.

before: She broke her heel at the party.
after: She broke the heel of her shoe.
accepted.reason: She broke her heel normally describes a bodily injury, while каблук is the heel of a shoe.
The English is improved, but Russian requires instrumental обильным or short-form обилен after был.
The proposal maps the plural noun корточки to a verb and no longer teaches the phrase-level noun correspondence.
